facts.statement: The DE single-player scenario lobby does not expose the random-map Victory dropdown; fixture victory behavior must be authored in the scenario.

Scenario unit rotation is a type-dependent per-object slot, not always a geometric angle. Confirmed examples: INDIANSTATUES uses integer rotation values as artwork indices across sixteen single-frame angle variants, while Gaia fish units use rotation as an animation-frame/phase selector; ordinary mobile units still use radian facing angles. Authoring consequence: variant-selecting types reward deliberate artwork diversity, while animation-frame types reward deliberate phase choices and tooling must not treat shared phase as under-use.

facts.statement: XS include directives resolve from the deployed XS module tree, not by embedding arbitrary sibling source inside the scenario.
XS constants or globals referenced across files must be declared with extern in the shared module.
Scenario trigger script_call stores the function call source in the effect message field, not in a separate xs_function scenario field.
XS file I/O can read a sidecar written by another scenario using the bare scenario/file stem convention.
XS sidecar writes are observable after close/flush behavior; partial files may exist if a fixture ends before writing its footer.

DAT effect command type 1 resource_modifier and type 6 resource_multiplier apply to the player when their containing technology is invoked by scenario research effects. In DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3, XS sidecar rows showed P1 resources moving from 0/0/0/0 to food=1111, wood=100, gold=222, and then wood=300 after the multiplier command.

DAT effect command types 0, 4, and 5 can set, add to, and multiply unit hit points when invoked through scenario research effects. In DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3, a normal villager castle-fire control disappeared while a villager spawned after set/add/multiply HP commands remained present through the later sidecar check; this proves runtime survival behavior, not direct raw HP values.

facts.statement: Scenario create_object can create a unit even when that unit is disabled in the player's civ availability table. In DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3, a P1 scout created before the enable_unit technology was researched and a second scout created after it; this proves trigger creation bypasses availability and does not prove UI trainability.

Scenario research-technology effects with force=0 can still invoke a technology effect despite an intentionally unaffordable configured resource cost. In DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3, an unforced target technology with 9000 food cost added stone +777 while P1 food remained far below that cost, so this path is not a cost-gated UI-research oracle.

DAT set_tech_cost is effect command type 100; type 101 is the additive tech-cost modifier path. The DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3 expected ledger was corrected after the generated command decoded as type=100, A=target tech, B=resource, C=-1, D=amount.

DAT effect command type 202 is interpreted as multiply attribute for the local building instance where a type-32 building-specific technology was researched. This follows the official 200/201 local-building command family, the 0/4/5 set/add/multiply arithmetic pattern, and current-DE DAT rows such as Herbal Medicine garrison_heal_rate x6, Masonry/Architecture hit_points x1.1, and Conscription work_rate x1.33.

facts.statement: DAT effect command type 204 is interpreted as an advanced additive local-building attribute command used by current-DE emplacement-style rows. It carries local-building attribute deltas including scalar combat fields and packed attack/armor values such as 770=(3<<8)+2 pierce armor, 1026=(4<<8)+2 melee armor, and 771=(3<<8)+3 pierce attack.

facts.statement: DAT disable_tech can block a later scenario research attempt against the disabled target technology. In DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3, the positive-control target added stone to 2109, then disable_tech fired, and the disabled target attempt left stone unchanged at 2109.

DAT upgrade_unit did not transform units in the tested forced scenario-research path. In DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3, the type=3 command row 74->75 was structurally present and invoked, but sidecar rows showed militia=1/man-at-arms=0 before the command, militia=1/man-at-arms=0 after it, and a later create_object militia also remained militia.

DAT spawn_unit did not add units in the tested forced scenario-research path. In DAT Semantics Diagnostic Run 3, the type=7 spawn villager-at-Town-Center command row was structurally present and invoked while P1 Town Center count stayed stable at 1, but villager count stayed 1 instead of increasing by 2.

facts.statement: The replay lobby-chat parser observes a bounded recent lobby-chat buffer; current evidence supports a 51-line retained window.
Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_1 is the current stockpiled food+wood+stone+gold sum for the player row.
Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_2 tracks the current living object unit-type-id sum for the player row.
Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_6 tracks the current living object count for the player row.

Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_7 tracks the current checksum-counted object position sum as (x+y)*100. In the all-visible Kill Factory run, the trigger-created P2 Chu Ko Nu at tile (6,10) added +1700, matching center coordinates (6.5+10.5)*100; the desync p0-sync object dump independently exposes the same XY100 aggregate candidate.
Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_8 carries the player number for the row.
Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_10 tracks a current living object instance-id sum for the player row.
A checksum object-count removal is evidence that an object disappeared from a player's current object set; it is not by itself a death, kill, raze, or player-caused action.

Under normal fog, AoE2DE can add counted vision-marker objects to replay op=2 checksum rows. In the Kill Factory A/B, the fog-on run added three unit 112 fog-reveal marker objects to P1 and P2 rows (+336 unit-type sum, +3 objects), while the all-visible run had zero unit 112 objects and P1 remained exactly one Castle object throughout.

A player flare ping is represented in replay checksum rows as unit 274 FLARE2 and is counted once in every target player's row for the sampling window. In the all-visible Kill Factory run, a single P1 flare targeting players 1-4 produced simultaneous +274 unit-type sum, +3 word_3, and +15 word_4 in all four rows.

A unit death need not decrement replay checksum object count immediately. In the Kill Factory run, unit 73 CHUKN became unit 28 CHUKN_D, producing a unit-type-sum delta of -45 with no object-count decrement; the later corpse expiration is the separate disappearance event.

Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_4 is the sum of the per-object carry field for the row's current checksum-counted objects. The field is generic: villagers use carry for held resources, monks for faith, flares/markers for lifetime, and corpses/rubble for decay timer. In the 500473166 desync comparison, P1 log carry_sum was 1972 versus replay word_4 1935 across a 9.152s gap; P2 log carry_sum was 829, and subtracting the KIPCHAK_D corpse carry of 297 gives 532 versus replay word_4 527.

Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_4 is not the raw sum of object retargetTimer values. In the 500473166 desync rough comparison, P1's nearest replay word_4 was 1935 while the first sync-log P1 retargetTimer sum was 303693.

Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_4 is not a raw active research/training timer sum in the Silent Frontier probe. P1 Feudal research ran from 00:11:01 to 00:13:11 while word_4 stayed at 0 across every checksum sample in that window; later dense unit-queue/research windows around 00:38:03-00:42:04 kept word_4 flat at 25 while other object aggregate words moved.

Trigger-driven object hit point changes did not affect the replay op=2 checksum matrix in the pavilion HP control: a P1 unit 626 pavilion was repeatedly modified by +19 HP and reached 1469 HP in the UI while the player's checksum object words stayed frozen across 36 samples.

Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_3 is best explained as the sum of the engine per-object state field for the player's current objects. Normal living objects mostly contribute state=2; flares/markers contribute state=3; corpse/rubble rows observed in the 500473166 desync log contribute state=5, so the +3 death-replacement fixture delta is the live-to-corpse state delta (5-2), not the corpse's absolute state.

The 500473166 desync p0-sync object dump exposed a concrete object-state census: state=2 appeared on 5672 rows and is the normal living-object state; state=3 appeared on 318 FLARE rows with hp=0; state=5 appeared on 70 hp=0 rows dominated by _D corpses, with a few zero-carry projectile rows also present. States 0, 4, 7, and 8 were rare in this artifact and remain uncharacterized.

In the Dawn Accord manual kill probe, rows narrated as defeated stopped changing checksum word_2 and word_6 after the defeat window while another checksum word continued periodic drift; this is a defeat-state signature candidate, not defeat proof.

In the Bohemond of Taranto spaced manual kill probe, decoded replay checksum rows bracket victim-side object lifecycle changes, but no decoded P1 checksum word behaved as a clean killer-side kill counter and victim row deltas did not reliably equal narrated unit-type IDs.

In the v15 Castle Kill Ground Truth run, the XS sidecar showed P1 credited kills attr20 moving 0->1->2->3, but no P1 replay op=2 checksum word mirrored that sequence; word_8 remained the player number and only false-matched while attr20 was 1.

In the v15 Castle Kill Ground Truth run, XS player attribute 20 tracked P1 total credited kills and the directed kill attributes agreed with victim incoming-from-P1 attr326 for actual credited kills: P1 vs P3 = P3 attr326 = 1 and P1 vs P4 = P4 attr326 = 2; P2 killed-by-others attr154 reached 2 while P2 attr326 stayed 0, showing attr154 is not directed killed-by-P1.

In the v16 Semantic Promotion run, P1 aggregate kills attr20 ended at 8 while the fixture's expected kill column was 4 after uncontrolled wandering-unit noise. P1 directed outgoing counters attr302/303/304 ended 1/2/1 and exactly matched victim incoming-from-P1 attr326 for P2/P3/P4, showing the directed counters were narrower than aggregate attr20 in this noisy engine run. The victim distribution did not match the original plan, so this supports directed-counter robustness, not exact fixture execution.

In the Emperor Romanos II all-visible visible-score probe, replay checksum word_9 did not match displayed player score or one fixed displayed-score scale; P1 visible score rose 1040->1187 while P1 word_9 moved 2098->1966, and defeated enemy rows used sentinel-like word_9 values near 0xFFFFFFFF while visible scores floored at the all-visible exploration component of 1000.

In the Dawn Accord autoscout/fog probe, P1's position-linked checksum word_7 froze during the narrated autoscout-off window, but P1 word_9 still changed 1019->1204->1145; word_9 is therefore not explained solely by movement or exploration drift.

Two independent POV recordings of the same ranked multiplayer match produced identical replay op=2 checksum matrices for every checksum sample, player row, and word 0..10 when report-local path fields were ignored. This proves the tested multiplayer checksum matrix is synced simulation state rather than local camera/input state.

AoE2DE desync p0-sync logs expose local client-computed object state in text form, including object name, instance id, dbid, hp, x/y/z position, state, carry, actionType, actionState, and retargetTimer inside per-player object dumps.

AoE2DE desync p0-sync logs expose a per-player Attributes block that declares a 601-wide player attribute array, but the 500473166 artifact printed only indices 0, 1, 2, and 3 in each of 20 player blocks. Attr20 kills, attr154 deaths, and directed kill/death attributes were not printed in this artifact.

Replay op=2 checksum matrix word_1 is supported by engine text output as the sum of player attributes 0..3, the food/wood/stone/gold stockpile. In the 500473166 desync rough comparison, P1's printed attr0..3 sum was 1090.697 versus replay word_1 1538 in the nearest prior checksum sample 9.152 seconds earlier; the comparison is directional rather than exact because the windows do not overlap.

AoE2DE desync p0-sync logs expose eight separately named RNG streams in text form: Action, World, AI, Object, Player, Editor, Comm, and UI, with SetSeed and Rand events tied to engine callsite labels and line numbers.

In the 500473166 desync fixture, two POV replay files had identical op=2 checksum matrices after ignoring report-local source offsets, while the p0-sync text log exposed later local-computation state. Replay cross-POV diffing alone cannot diagnose this desync class.

In the Emperor Romanos II all-visible visible-score probe, defeated players' visible scores floored at exactly 1000 for both Red and Yellow; this is the 100 percent explored endpoint of the exploration score component, not a universal defeat constant.

AoE2DE score includes an exploration component of 10 points per percent map explored. Evidence: the all-visible Romanos defeat floor was 1000 at 100 percent explored, and the fogged Shahanshah Kavadh postgame screens showed Technology/exploration score 40 at 4 percent explored and 10 at 1 percent explored.

AoE2DE postgame Statistics Technology score includes the exploration component: in the Shahanshah Kavadh fogged score probe, Research Count was 0 for all players while Technology score was 40/10/10/10 for Percent Map Explored 4/1/1/1.

AoE2DE postgame Statistics screens can show per-player score components, kills/losses, research count, and percent map explored even when the recorded replay op=6 postgame payload contains only metadata/leaderboard/world-time blocks and no serialized per-player stats.

AoE2DE's in-game score display appears to use X/Y as own score / combined team score; this is consistent with chrae's fogged score screenshot transcription and the prior team-score mean observations, but still needs a deliberately nontrivial team composition probe before engine_verified promotion.
In the Emperor Romanos II visible-score probe, the displayed allied team score matched floor(mean(member visible scores)) across six score readings.
